correctness.rationale: Bracket equals det(x,y,z)e1; multilinearity reduces the embedding equation to det(T)det(x,y,z)e1=det(Tx,Ty,z)Te1. For rank <=1 both sides vanish. For rank 2 one can choose Tx,Ty independent, hence Te1 must vanish, which suffices. For rank 3, substituting z=Tw and using nondegenerate determinant forces T=scalar identity, and conversely scalar maps satisfy equation. Rank-count formula counts ordered independent columns 2,3 for rank 2. Direct independent exhaustive maps over F2 and F3 respectively gave (1,49,42,1) and (1,338,624,2), total 93/965; these only corroborate the all-field rank proof. Extension-field polynomial yields zeta by the standard exponential generating formula. Characteristic two is covered by alternating determinant algebra; classification is for this chosen model, not all such algebras.

value.rationale: This determines the entire rank-stratified moduli set of a canonical nontrivial three-dimensional 3-Lie model, including finite-field point polynomial and zeta. The one-term versus cyclic-three-term distinction is mathematically meaningful and cannot be inferred from existing O-operator tables. residual_risks: The work is a small-model classification, not a structure theorem for arbitrary 3-Lie algebras.

final_claim: For the fixed alternating three-dimensional 3-Lie algebra with [e1,e2,e3]=e1 over every field, adjoint embedding tensors are exactly rank<=1 maps, rank-2 maps killing e1, and invertible scalar maps. Over F_q the rank counts are 1,(q-1)(q^2+q+1)^2,(q^3-1)(q^3-q),q-1; total q^6+q^5-q^2+q-1 and zeta function (1-q^2t)(1-t)/((1-q^6t)(1-q^5t)(1-qt)).
